_doc: Hand-written golden-plan overrides (docs/eval/GOLDEN_EVALS_SPEC.md 4.1). scripts/golden/build_fixtures.py only reads this file. An override replaces the template CAUSE and/or FIX when the template leaks gold code, a gold-only name, or hidden-test content. It describes the change in words, may use names from the issue or the original repository, and never contains new code. The leak rules run again on the final plan; the build fails if any violation remains.

fastapi_13920.CAUSE: analyze_param only looks for Depends, Query and similar markers when the parameter's annotation has Annotated as its origin; a PEP 695 alias is a TypeAliasType object that hides its Annotated value, so the marker is never seen and the parameter becomes a required query parameter.
fastapi_13920.FIX: At the top of analyze_param, when the annotation is a type alias (the is_typealiastype check the issue names, from the typing-inspection package), replace it with the alias's value before any other inspection.
fastapi_13920.why: template FIX names the new import module; CAUSE shared an added-line fragment

fastapi_14258.CAUSE: include_router never checks whether the router passed in is the router itself, so including a router into itself loops over its own routes while appending to them and hangs the process.
fastapi_14258.FIX: At the start of include_router, before the prefix checks, fail with an assertion error (like the method's other argument checks) when the router to include is self, with a clear message that a router may not contain itself.
fastapi_14258.why: template FIX quoted the gold assert and its message

fastapi_14301.CAUSE: get_parameterless_sub_dependant, used for dependencies declared on routes, routers and the app, calls get_dependant without forwarding depends.scope so a function-scoped dependency declared there falls back to the default request scope.
fastapi_14301.FIX: In get_parameterless_sub_dependant, forward depends.scope to get_dependant through its scope keyword, next to the path, call and security scopes it already passes.
fastapi_14301.why: template FIX was the gold keyword argument verbatim

fastapi_14306.CAUSE: Feature, not a bug: request, websocket and response validation errors carried only their error list, and only the response one had a string form, so server logs could not tell which endpoint raised a validation error.
fastapi_14306.FIX: Give the ValidationException family an optional keyword argument holding the endpoint's function, path, file and line (a typing.TypedDict), a singular or plural string form in the base class that appends that location, and pass it from routing wherever these errors are raised.
fastapi_14306.why: template FIX named the gold-only keyword argument

fastapi_14372.CAUSE: The Depends class and its Security subclass are plain dataclasses with equality, so Python sets their hash to None and hashing one raises TypeError, which breaks tools that store them in sets or dicts.
fastapi_14372.FIX: Make both dataclasses frozen so Python generates a value-based hash, and change analyze_param, which assigns the dependency on a copied Depends, to build a modified copy with the replace function of the dataclasses module instead.
fastapi_14372.why: template FIX was the gold decorator and call verbatim

fastapi_14458.CAUSE: is_gen_callable, is_async_gen_callable and is_coroutine_callable fall back to inspecting the callable's __call__ attribute, so a class whose instances define an async or generator __call__ is itself treated as a coroutine or generator.
fastapi_14458.FIX: In each of the three properties, after the direct function checks and before the dunder_call fallback, return False when the unwrapped callable is a class: calling a class only builds an instance.
fastapi_14458.why: template FIX was the gold if-statement verbatim

fastapi_14479.CAUSE: In analyze_param the Query branch asserts that the field is a supported query type with no message, so an unsupported query annotation fails at startup with an empty AssertionError that names nothing.
fastapi_14479.FIX: Give that bare assert a message that names the offending query parameter (its name in repr form) and says its type is not supported; change nothing else.
fastapi_14479.why: template CAUSE quoted the assert; template FIX was the gold message

fastapi_14487.why: template FIX quoted the gold message text

fastapi_14851.CAUSE: An upcoming upstream release drops the deprecated on_event machinery that APIRouter inherits, so on_event, the matching constructor arguments and lifespans written as generator functions would stop working.
fastapi_14851.FIX: Move that machinery into APIRouter itself: keep the startup and shutdown callables in lists on the router, register them from on_event, supply a fallback lifespan object that calls them, and wrap generator-function lifespans, instead of inheriting any of it.
fastapi_14851.why: template named Starlette internals the gold vendors

fastapi_15588.CAUSE: ServerSentEvent only rejects NUL characters in id; event and id values that contain a carriage return or a newline are written verbatim as SSE field lines, so a multi-line value injects extra fields or events.
fastapi_15588.FIX: Validate event and id with pydantic after-validators that raise ValueError for a value containing a carriage return or a newline, with a message in the style of the existing null-character message that names the field.

fastapi_9555.CAUSE: The is_gen_callable, is_async_gen_callable and is_coroutine_callable cached properties inspect the dependency callable directly, so a wrapped (functools.wraps) async or generator function is misclassified.
fastapi_9555.FIX: Unwrap the dependency callable once (follow __wrapped__, as the unwrap helper of the stdlib inspect module does) in a new cached property, and use it in all three is-callable properties.
fastapi_9555.why: template FIX named the gold-only property and call

fastapi_9753.CAUSE: The cached _unwrapped_call property follows __wrapped__ but not functools.partial, so a partial of an async or generator function is misclassified.
fastapi_9753.FIX: In _unwrapped_call, after following __wrapped__, also strip functools.partial layers by taking each partial's underlying func.
